result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` now counts as test mock resources, whatever follows, at any depth and with backslash paths too. The new tests pass (3 in `ScopingConventionsTest`, 6 in `SourceFileFilterTest`), and nothing is committed.

- **`ScopingConventions.java`**: the two mock rules (`__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/` and `mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/`) are replaced by one rule, `.*/(__)?mock[^/]*/.*`. The `[^/]*` lets the folder name carry any characters, including punctuation and non-ASCII, while still stopping at the folder boundary. The existing `mockapi`, `[Mm]ocks`, and `_mock.*` rules are unchanged, so `mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/` and `mockStore/` stay test code.
- **`ScopingConventionsTest.java`** (new, under `src/test/.../sourcecode/scoping/`): three tests covering the new cases, the folders that must stay test code, and the non-matches (`remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, `mock.java`, `mockery.java`).

I didn't re-run the Sokrates scan on the elasticsearch tree, so the 2,500-line count is unverified.
